subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw move memoryFlush and preflight compaction into a dedicated/preemptible maintenance lane, or keep them in-band with shorter timeouts and watchdog recovery?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and high impact, but the durable fix changes scheduler and session-state ordering semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Dedicated Maintenance Lane
options.body: Move memoryFlush and compaction out of the foreground reply lane while preserving transcript rotation and active-run invariants.

options.title: In-Band With Watchdog
options.body: Keep the current lane ownership but add faster abort, stuck-lane recovery, and user-visible diagnostics.

options.title: Timeout Mitigation Only
options.body: Treat the 180s default timeout and current notices as sufficient and leave lane isolation out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Dedicated Maintenance Lane
recommendation.body: Move memoryFlush and compaction out of the foreground reply lane while preserving transcript rotation and active-run invariants.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the memoryFlush feature and is the strongest history-backed routing candidate for the scheduler/product choice.
